lesson.title: Learn: make an adverb clause shorter

items.title: Clause → phrase
lines: Cut the subject and be. Or cut the subject and use -ing.
chips: While I was walking to class, I ran into an old friend. → While walking to class, I ran into an old friend.
Before I left for work, I ate breakfast. → Before leaving for work, I ate breakfast.

items.text: Before I left for work, I ate breakfast. → Before ___ for work, I ate breakfast.
options: left
leaving
leave

items.title: Same subject only
lines: The phrase describes the subject of the main clause.
chips: ✅ While sitting in class, Ann fell asleep. (Ann was sitting)
❌ While watching TV last night, the phone rang. (The phone was watching TV?)

items.text: While the teacher was lecturing to the class, I fell asleep. Can you shorten it?
options: Yes: While lecturing to the class, I fell asleep.
No. The subjects are different.

items.text: Which is correct?
options: While sitting at my computer, the fire alarm went off.
While sitting at my computer, I heard the fire alarm go off.
items.why: I was sitting, not the fire alarm.

lines: Same subject in both clauses → you can shorten: While walking to class, I…
Different subjects → no change. (No “dangling” phrases!)

levels.full: Changing Time Clauses to Modifying Adverbial Phrases

lesson.title: Learn: after, before, when, while, since + -ing

items.title: Five time words
lines: after / before / when / while / since + -ing.
chips: Since coming to this country, Maria has made many friends.
When cooking, Tyrell uses a lot of spices.
After finishing his homework, Peter went to bed.

items.text: Since Maria came to this country, she has made many friends. → Since ___ to this country, Maria has made many friends.
options: came
coming

items.title: Put the name in the main clause
lines: The phrase has no subject, so the main clause needs the noun.
chips: When Tyrell cooks, he uses a lot of spices. → When cooking, Tyrell uses a lot of spices.

items.title: After finishing = After having finished
lines: No difference in meaning. The phrase can also come last.
chips: After finishing his homework, Peter went to bed.
After having finished his homework, Peter went to bed.
Peter went to bed after finishing his homework.

items.text: ___ to this country, I have experienced some interesting cultural traditions.
options: Since came
Since coming

items.text: After Karl had been climbing for several hours, his muscles began to ache. Can you shorten it?
options: Yes
No. Karl ≠ his muscles.

lines: after / before / when / while / since + verb-ing (same subject).
After finishing = After having finished. The phrase can come first or last.

examples.text: Since coming to this country, Maria has made many friends.

talk.title: Before going to bed…
talk.task: Claude asks: What do you do before going to bed? After waking up? While sitting in class?
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. Ask me one question at a time: What do you do before going to bed? after waking up? after arriving at school or work? while sitting in class? before leaving for the day? while preparing for a difficult exam? I answer in complete sentences that reuse the phrase (Before going to bed, I always ...). Check that I use -ing after before/after/while and that the subject of my main clause is the person doing both actions.

items.title: You can drop while
lines: An -ing phrase at the start can mean “during that time.”

items.title: The subject rule still works
lines: The -ing phrase always describes the subject after the comma.

options: Walking

lines: -ing phrase + comma + subject: Walking down the street, I ran into an old friend.

items.title: -ing = because
lines: Drop because and the subject. Use -ing.

Because lacking

items.title: Having + participle = because + before
lines: It happened earlier.
chips: Having seen that movie before, I don't want to go again.
Not having tasted the soup, she didn't realize how bad it was.

items.title: be → Being (or nothing)
lines: Being makes the reason clear.
chips: Because he is a doctor, Oskar often gets calls at night. → Being a doctor, Oskar often gets calls at night.

talk.title: Advice before going abroad
talk.task: Your friend has never traveled abroad. Give advice: “Before leaving on your trip, …”
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English speaking partner. A friend of mine is traveling to a foreign country for the first time. Give me one sentence beginning at a time and I finish it with advice: Before leaving on your trip, ... / Upon arriving at the airport, ... / After getting to your destination, ... / When talking with the local people, ... / While visiting tourist sites, ... / Before leaving for home, .... Check that the subject of my main clause is 'you' (or an imperative), so the phrase is not dangling.

talk.title: Write a summary
talk.task: Summarize a short story (like the QWERTY keyboard) in 4-5 sentences with short -ing phrases.
talk.claudePrompt: You are my English writing partner. Give me a short factual passage of 6-8 simple sentences (an invention, a discovery, an animal). I write a 4-5 sentence summary that includes at least three modifying phrases (While ...ing, After ...ing, Upon ...ing, Having ..., ...ing). Check: only essential information; the phrase and the main clause have the same subject; a comma after a phrase that comes first; not every sentence is reduced.
